class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <h2 id="3.-Neural-network:-Time-dependent-U-Net">3. Neural network: Time-dependent U-Net<a class="anchor-link" href="#3.-Neural-network:-Time-dependent-U-Net">¶</a></h2> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=eb99f4cf-d5af-4277-966b-71f4ec2cb7ad"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Next, we need to define our denoising network $\epsilon_{\theta}(x_t,t)$. As we operate on images, a natural choice is a <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/1505.04597.pdf">U-Net</a>: <img alt="image.png" src="data:image/png;base64,"/></p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=550beee0-4e1b-4b9c-902e-4a49ef8c23a5"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>A U-Net is a good choice as it <strong>maps an image</strong> $x$ (i.e. a tensor of shape $[c,h,w]$ where $c$ is the number of channels and $h,w$ the height and width in pixels) <strong>to a tensor of the same shape</strong> using only convolutions, i.e. respecting the spatial structure of the image. Such a tensor of shape $[c,h,w]$ is usually called a <strong>multi-channel feature map</strong> as it assigns a pixel location a feature of $c$ dimensions.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=16efb414-7a46-4865-b36a-019e84d1bf47"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>A U-Net is a <strong>fully convolutional neural network</strong>, i.e. there is no fully connected layer but only convolutions (in addition to non-linearities and pooling layers that have no learnable parameters). It has a special “residual” structure of a contractual and an expansive path giving it that U-shape above. The contractual path is simply a standard convolutional neural network with any padding, i.e. the width and height of the image tensor decrease (from 572x572 to 30x30) while the number of channels (the $c$) increases. The expansive path uses <a href="https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51605006/how-does-upsampling-in-fully-connected-convolutional-network-work">upsampling</a>, i.e. creating a higher resolution tensor from a lower resolution one artifically. Every previous tensor is upsampled and a cropped version of the corresponding multi-channel feature map from the contractive path is added.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=f07824e2-945b-4160-a929-f9a2aa3415b2"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>It is not straight-forward though as we have to adopt a U-Net slightly to account for the fact that we need a time-dependent output $\epsilon_{\theta}(x_t,t)$. To do so, we add a <strong>time embedding</strong> that embeds time into a $d$-dimensional vector to the overall U-Net: \begin{align*} E(t) = A\cdot\text{softmax}(\tau(t-t_1)^2,\dots, \tau(t-t_n)^2)+b \end{align*} where $A$ is a learnable matrix and $b$ a bias vector and $\tau$ a temperature parameter and $t_1,\dots,t_n$ are evenly spaced time points in $[0,T]$. For each block of the contractive and expanding path, we then add a fully connected neural network to map $E(t)$ to a $c$-dimensional vector where $c$ is the number of channels of that block. We then simply add the embedding to the feature map and apply a non-linearity.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noOutputs" jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>In this tutorial, we are going to apply the theory Ito SDEs that we discussed in the <a href="https://www.peterholderrieth.com/blog/2023/Diffusion-Models-with-Stochastic-Differential-Equations-A-Introduction-with-Self-Contained-Mathematical-Proofs/">last tutorial</a>. We are going to implement the Ito SDE with affine drift coefficients to build a diffusion model and use it to sample from a <strong>simple</strong> distribution. Using a simple distribution allows to learn a lot about the inner workings of diffusion models, while still doing all the heavy lifting for implementing diffusion models for when we apply them to images. In the next tutorial, we are then going to apply these structures on images and scale it up.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" Load Dataset<a class="anchor-link" href="#1.-Load-Dataset">¶</a></h2> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=f5b00240-e902-488f-b933-0a0997f47a04"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Let's build a very simple distribution in 2d that modulates a real-world scenario. Real-world data often lies on a manifold in a high-dimensional space (this is also called the <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manifold_hypothesis">Manifold hypothesis</a>). For example, the set of all possible images does not cover any combination of pixel values but rather a subset that does cover full pixel space. We simulate such a scenario in 2d by making our data lie on a 1-dimensional manifold, i.e. a curve. We define a simple manifold defined by the quadratic function.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=a4e61019-d634-48e0-a416-741f19976763"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"> <div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt">In [38]:</div> <div class="jp-CodeMirrorEditor jp-Editor jp-InputArea-editor" data-type="inline"> <div class="cm-editor cm-s-jupyter"> <div class="highlight hl-ipython3"><pre><span></span><span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">manifold_func</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="p">):</span> <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">**</span><span class="mi">2</span>

Define SDE<a class="anchor-link" href="#2.-Define-SDE">¶</a></h2> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=472c492f-8b64-4089-84c8-278a29aafa11"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Next, we define an abstract class representation an Ito Stochastic Differental Equation: $$dX_t = f(X_t,t)dt + g(t)dW_t$$</p> <p>The class requires you to specify:</p> <ol> <li><code>cond_exp</code>: the conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}[X_t|X_0]$</li> <li><code>cond_var</code>: the conditional variance $\mathbb{V}[X_t|X_0]$</li> <li><code>f_drift</code>: the drift function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^d$.</li> <li><code>g_random</code>: the infinitesimal variance $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$.</li> </ol> <p>Moreover, it has functions that evolve the SDE forward and backward. We assume throughout this chapter that conditional expectations and variances $\mathbb{E}[X_t|X_0], \mathbb{V}[X_t|X_0]$ can be analytically computed and that conditional distributions are Gaussian. This is in particular true for ItoSDEs for affine drift coefficients as we have seen.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noOutputs" id="cell-id=36e8b04c-d3ee-46ea-b917-7e071c3b677f"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"> <div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt">In [40]:</div> <div class="jp-CodeMirrorEditor jp-Editor jp-InputArea-editor" data-type="inline"> <div class="cm-editor cm-s-jupyter"> <div class="highlight hl-ipython3"><pre><span></span><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">ItoSDE</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ABC</span><span class="p">):</span> <span class="k">def</span> <span class="fm">__init__</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">T_max</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span><span class="p">):</span> <span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">T_max</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">T_max</span>
<span class="nd">@abstractmethod</span> <span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">cond_exp</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">X_0</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">):</span> <span class="k">pass</span>
<span class="nd">@abstractmethod</span> <span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">cond_var</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">X_0</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">):</span> <span class="k">pass</span>
<span class="nd">@abstractmethod</span> <span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">f_drift</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">X_t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">):</span> <span class="k">pass</span>
<span class="nd">@abstractmethod</span> <span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">g_random</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">X_t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">):</span> <span class="k">pass</span>
<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">cond_std</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">X_0</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">):</span> <span class="w"> </span><span class="sd">"""Conditional standard deviation. Square root of self.cond_var."""</span> <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">torch</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sqrt</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cond_var</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">X_0</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">X_0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">))</span>

<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">run_forward</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">self</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">X_0</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Tensor</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">clip_factor</span><span data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <h3 id="2.1--Variance-preserving-SDE">2.1 Variance-preserving SDE<a class="anchor-link" href="#2.1--Variance-preserving-SDE">¶</a></h3> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=cdb203ec-5a9f-428c-b75e-2b7eaa5e7892"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Let's implement the variance-preserving SDE that is the basis for the <a href="https://proceedings.mlr.press/v37/sohl-dickstein15.html">first formulation of diffusion models</a> with:</p> <ol> <li>$f(x,t)=-\frac{1}{2}x\beta'(t)$</li> <li>$g=\sqrt{\beta'(t)}$</li> <li>$\beta(t)=t\beta_{\text{min}}+\frac{1}{2}t^2(\beta_{\text{max}}-\beta_{\text{min}})$</li> <li>$\beta'(t)=\beta_{\text{min}}+t(\beta_{\text{max}}-\beta_{\text{min}})$</li> <li>$\mathbb{E}[X_t|X_0] = \exp(-0.5\beta(t))$</li> <li>$\mathbb{V}[X_t|X_0] = 1-\exp(\beta(t))$</li> </ol> <p>I.e. the expectation exponentially decays to $0$ while the <em>conditional</em> variance converges to one - the variance $\mathbb{V}[X_t]=1$ if we assume that the data is normalized to variance 1 (see the <a href="https://www.peterholderrieth.com/blog/2023/Diffusion-Models-with-Stochastic-Differential-Equations-A-Introduction-with-Self-Contained-Mathematical-Proofs/">last tutorial</a> for an explanation and derivation).</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noOutputs" id="cell-id=f5009732-bd49-41c5-b4b8-799ca86edef1"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" Neural network<a class="anchor-link" href="#3.-Neural-network">¶</a></h2> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=37b60751-e543-4d8e-a2cc-d8319684cb2c"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Next, we define the neural network that we need to train. As we have seen in the last tutorial, there are two options: we can either train a neural network $s_{\theta}(x_t,t)$ to approximate a score $\nabla_{x_t} \log p_t(x_t|x_0)$ or we can train a neural network $\epsilon_{\theta}(x_t,t)$ to predict the noise an image has been distored. Both cases are related:</p> <p>$$ \begin{align*}&\epsilon_{\theta}(x_t,t)=-s_{\theta}(x_t,t)\sqrt{\mathbb{V}[X_t|X_0=x_0]}\\ \Leftrightarrow &s_{\theta}(x_t,t)=-\frac{\epsilon_\theta(x_t,t)}{\sqrt{\mathbb{V}[X_t|X_0=x_0]}}\end{align*}$$</p> <p>where $\mathbb{V}[X_t|X_0]=1-\exp(-\beta(t))$.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell" id="cell-id=95308d73-9b8b-4ab3-a35c-59931caa285f"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper" tabindex="0"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>I introduce a flag <code>TRAIN_SCORE</code> that you can set to switch between both options. Consistent with <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.11239.pdf">literature</a>, I found that training the denoising network leads to more stable training and therefore we train a neural network $\epsilon_{\theta}(x_t,t)$ but feel free it.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noOutputs" id="cell-id=8bd49e8d-210e-44d1-9f89-fd3c39690d55"> <div jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput" data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Finally, let's run SDE backwards with the <a href="https://www.peterholderrieth.com/blog/2023/Diffusion-Models-with-Stochastic-Differential-Equations-A-Introduction-with-Self-Contained-Mathematical-Proofs/">equation that we derived</a>: $$\begin{align*}&d\bar{X}_t= [f(X_t,t)-g^2(t)s_{\theta}(x,t)dt + g(t)d\bar{W}_t\\ \Leftrightarrow& \bar{X}_{t-s} \approx \bar{X}_t -s\left[g^2(t)\frac{\epsilon_{\theta}(\bar{X}_t,t)}{\sqrt{1-\exp(-\beta(t))}}+f(\bar{X}_t,t)\right]+\sqrt{s}g(t)\epsilon \quad \text{ where } \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)\end{align*}$$</p> <p>where we clip the denominator $\sqrt{1-\exp(-\beta(t))}$ to avoid numerical instability when the denonimator is close to zero:</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell class="sd">"""Function to run stochastic differential equation. We assume a deterministic initial distribution p_0."""</span> <span class="n">model</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">model</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">device</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="c1">#Number of trajectories, dimension of data:</span> <span class="n">n_traj</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">x_start</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">shape</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="n">ndim</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">x_start</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">dim</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span>
<span class="c1">#Compute time grid for discretization and step size:</span> <span class="n">time_grid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">torch</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">linspace</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">sde</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">T_max</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_steps</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="n">step_size</span> <span class="o">=</span><span class="n">torch</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">abs</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">])</span>
<span class="c1">#Compute the random drift at every time point:</span> <span class="n">random_drift_grid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">sde</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">g_random</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="c1">#Sample random drift at every time point:</span> <span class="n">noise</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">torch</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">randn</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n_steps</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="nb">list</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x_start</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">shape</span><span class="p">)))</span> <span class="n">random_drift_grid_sample</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">torch</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sqrt</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">step_size</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">noise</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">random_drift_grid</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">view</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ndim</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">))</span>
<span class="c1">#Initialize list of trajectory:</span> <span class="n">x_traj</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">x_start</span><span class="p">]</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">plot_evolution</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">fig</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">axs</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">plt</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">subplots</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="n">figsize</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">))</span>
<span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">time</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">tqdm</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">enumerate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">)):</span>
<span class="c1">#Get last location and time</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="n">t</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="n">time_vec</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">repeat</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n_traj</span><span class="p">)</span>

<span class="c1">#Get random drift:</span> <span class="n">random_drift_sample</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">random_drift_grid_sample</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span>

    </script> </head> <body class="jp-Notebook" data-jp-theme-light="true" data-jp-theme-name="JupyterLab Light"> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <h1 id="A-Self-Contained-Tutorial-on-Ito-Stochastic-Differential-Equations-for-Diffusion-Models">A Self-Contained Tutorial on Ito Stochastic Differential Equations for Diffusion Models<a class="anchor-link" href="#A-Self-Contained-Tutorial-on-Ito-Stochastic-Differential-Equations-for-Diffusion-Models">¶</a></h1> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>In the machine learning community in the context of Diffusion Models, there has been a big interest in Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) recently. SDEs are a powerful concept driving powerful generative AI tools from image generation (see <a href="https://openai.com/dall-e-2">DALL-E-2</a> or <a href="https://stablediffusionweb.com/">Stable Diffusion</a>) to protein generation (see <a href="https://www.bakerlab.org/2023/07/11/diffusion-model-for-protein-design/">RF-Diffusion</a>). However, the accompanying papers assume understanding of complex results from the theory of SDEs - such as the time-reversal formula. As a result, the works are more and more inaccessible for non-SDE experts. This blog post aims to help out here and give a self-contained introduction to SDEs for diffusion models. <strong>All mathematical results for SDEs that are used for diffusion models are proven here.</strong> More specifically, in this tutorial, you will know:</p> <ol> <li>What SDEs are.</li> <li>How SDEs are implemented.</li> <li>The distribution and convergence properties of SDEs with affine drift coefficients.</li> <li>An overview of famous diffusion models and how they can be framed as SDEs with affine drift coefficients.</li> <li>How SDEs can be time-reversed and how that corresponds to novel generation.</li> <li>How to train a diffusion model.</li> </ol> <p><strong>First time hear about SDEs?:</strong> If you have never heard about SDEs, I would recommend you to first read my <a href="INSERTLINK">previous tutorial</a> where I explore the <em>Langevin SDE</em> that is fundamental for machine learning.</p> <p><strong>More interested in practical implementations?</strong> in my <a href="">next tutorial</a>, we are going to put the theory into practice.</p> <p><strong>Required background:</strong> I assume that you have background knowledge in probability theory.</p> <p><strong>Acknowledgement:</strong> the content of this tutorial has partially grown out of several nights trying to understand the famous diffusion model SDE paper by <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2011.13456.pdf">Song et al.</a>.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noOutputs "> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div Introduction: What are Stochastic Differential Equations?<a class="anchor-link" href="#1.-Introduction:-What-are-Stochastic-Differential-Equations?">¶</a></h2><p>The solutions of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) is a <em>stochastic process</em>. A <strong>stochastic process</strong> is a collection of random variables $X_t\in\mathbb{R}^d$ that evolve over the time $t\geq 0$. While each $X_t$ is random for each individual $t$, the beauty of stochastic processes comes in studying how $X_{t+s}$ is related to $X_{t}$ - i.e. how values at different time points depend on each other.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <h3 id="1.1.-Stochastic-Processes-and-Brownian-Motion">1.1. Stochastic Processes and Brownian Motion<a class="anchor-link" href="#1.1.-Stochastic-Processes-and-Brownian-Motion">¶</a></h3><p>A fundamental stochastic process is a <strong>Brownian motion</strong> $W_t$. A Brownian motion is characterized by:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Normal increments:</strong> Increments are normally distributed with variance scaling proportional to the time difference: $W_{t+s}-W_{t}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,s\mathbf{I}_d)$ for all $t,s\geq 0$.</li> <li><strong>Independent increments:</strong> $W_{t_1}-W_{t_2}$ is independent of $W_{t_2}-W_{t_3}$ for $t_1>t_2>t_3$.</li> </ol> <p>We can sample trajectories of a Brownian motion by discretizing the stochastic process by: $$W_{t+s} = W_{t} +\sqrt{s} \epsilon\quad\text{where }\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$$</p> <p>Let's plot 5 trajectories:</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell "> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"> <div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt">In [2]:</div> <div class="jp-CodeMirrorEditor jp-Editor jp-InputArea-editor" data-type="inline"> <div class="CodeMirror cm-s-jupyter"> <div class=" highlight hl-ipython3"><pre><span></span><span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">run_brownian_motion</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n_traj</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">10000</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">t_start</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">t_end</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">10.0</span><span class="p">):</span>
    <span class="n">time_grid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">linspace</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">t_start</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">t_end</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">grid_size</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">t_end</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">t_start</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="n">n_grid_points</span>
    <span class="n">x_0</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">n_traj</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">]])</span>
    <span class="n">gaussian_noise</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">random</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">normal</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_traj</span><span class="p">))</span>
    <span class="n">brownian_motion</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sqrt</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">grid_size</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">gaussian_noise</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cumsum</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">axis</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">brownian_motion</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">concatenate</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">x_0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">brownian_motion</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="n">axis</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">brownian_motion</span>

<span class="n">fig</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">ax</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">plt</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">subplots</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">figsize</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">9</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">9</span><span class="p">))</span>
<span class="n">time</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">X_t</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">run_brownian_motion</span><span class="p">()</span>
<span class="n">sample_labels</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"Trajectory </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">i</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="nb">range</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">)]</span>
<span class="n">ax</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">plot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">X_t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">label</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">sample_labels</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="n">ax</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_xlabel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"time t"</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="n">ax</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_ylabel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"W_t"</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="n">ax</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">legend</span><span class="p">();</span>
</pre></div> </body></html> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell-outputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-OutputCollapser jp-Cell-outputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-OutputArea jp-Cell-outputArea"> <div class="jp-OutputArea-child"> <div class="jp-OutputPrompt jp-OutputArea-prompt"></div> <div class="jp-RenderedImage jp-OutputArea-output "> <img src="data:image/png;base64," class=" "> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p><em>If you feel reminded of a graph describing a stock market index, good guess! Brownian motion is <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownian_model_of_financial_markets">widely used in Mathematical Finance</a> to model stock prices.</em></p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <h3 id="1.2-From-Ordinary-Differential-Equations-to-Stochastic-Differential-Equations">1.2 From Ordinary Differential Equations to Stochastic Differential Equations<a class="anchor-link" href="#1.2-From-Ordinary-Differential-Equations-to-Stochastic-Differential-Equations">¶</a></h3> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>To understand SDE, let's start by reviewing the <strong>classical ordinary differential equations (ODEs)</strong>. An ODE is an equation with the following characteristics:</p> <ol> <li>Its solution $\mathbf{x}(t)$ is a deterministic function: $x:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^d$.</li> <li>The rate of change $$\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{x}(t) = f(\mathbf{x}(t),t)$$ is time- and location-dependent and given by a function $$f:\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^d,(\mathbf{x},t)\to f(\mathbf{x},t)$$.</li> <li>A fixed start value: $x(0)=v\in\mathbb{R}^d$.</li> </ol> <p>A <strong>Stochastic Differential Equation "is an ODE but just random"</strong>. In other words, an SDE is an equation with the following characteristics:</p> <ol> <li>Its solution $X_t$ is a stochastic process. I.e. a sample of a stochastic process is a function $t\to X_t\in\mathbb{R}^d$.</li> <li>The rate of change $$dX(t) = f(X_t,t)dt+g(t)dW_t$$ is given by <ul> <li><strong>A</strong>. A <em>deterministic</em> drift specified by a function $f$.</li> <li><strong>B</strong>. A <em>random</em> drift specified by a function $g\geq 0$ and a Brownian motion $W_t$.</li> </ul> </li> <li>A start distribution $X_0\sim p_0$.</li> </ol> <p>Intuitively, the above equation means that for (infinitisimally) small $s>0$, we have</p> $$X_{t+s}\approx X_{t}+s f(X_t,t)+g(t)\sqrt{s}(W_{t+s}-W_{t})$$<p>In other words, the conditional distribution for the next time step $X_{t+s}$ given the current time step $X_{t}$ is given by $$X_{t+s}|X_t\sim\mathcal{N}(X_{t}+s f(X_t,t),sg^2(t))$$</p> <p>So <strong>the deterministic drift $f$ describes the infinitesimal change in mean and the volatility function $g$ describes the infinitesimal standard deviation</strong>.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <h2 id="2.-Implementing-SDEs-with-the-Euler-Maruyama-method">2. Implementing SDEs with the Euler-Maruyama method<a class="anchor-link" href="#2.-Implementing-SDEs-with-the-Euler-Maruyama-method">¶</a></h2> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>In this section, we simulate SDEs and look at a few example SDEs.</p> <p>To simulate SDEs, we discretize them in time and then sampling the next time step with the above update rule:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Input:</strong> number of steps $n_{\text{steps}}$, step size $s>0$</li> <li>Sample $X_0\sim p_0$</li> <li>Set $t=0$</li> <li><p>For $i=1,...n_{\text{steps}}$:</p> <p>Sample $\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)$</p> <p>Set $X_{t+s} = X_{t} + sf(X_{t},t)+g(t)\sqrt{s}\epsilon$</p> </li> <li><strong>Return:</strong> $[X_{0},X_{s},X_{2s},X_{3s},\dots,X_{sn_{\text{steps}}}]$</li> </ul> <p>The above method is called the <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler%E2%80%93Maruyama_method">Euler-Maruyama method</a>.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noOutputs "> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"> <div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt">In [3]:</div> <div class="jp-CodeMirrorEditor jp-Editor jp-InputArea-editor" data-type="inline"> <div class="CodeMirror cm-s-jupyter"> <div class=" highlight hl-ipython3"><pre><span></span><span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">run_sde</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">f_determ_drift</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Callable</span><span class="p">,</span>
            <span class="n">g_random_drift</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Callable</span><span class="p">,</span>
            <span class="n">x_start</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">,</span>
            <span class="n">t_start</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> 
            <span class="n">t_end</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span> 
            <span class="n">n_steps</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">10000</span><span class="p">,</span>
            <span class="o">**</span><span class="n">kwargs</span><span class="p">):</span>
    <span class="sd">"""Function to run stochastic differential equation. We assume a deterministic initial distribution p_0."""</span>
    
    <span class="c1">#Number of trajectories, dimension of data:</span>
    <span class="n">n_traj</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">dim_x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">x_start</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">shape</span>

    <span class="c1">#Compute time grid for discretization and step size:</span>
    <span class="n">time_grid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">linspace</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">t_start</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">t_end</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_steps</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">step_size</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span>

    <span class="c1">#Compute the random drift at every time point:</span>
    <span class="n">random_drift_grid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">g_random_drift</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">)</span>
    
    <span class="c1">#Sample random drift at every time point:</span>
    <span class="n">noise</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">random</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">normal</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n_steps</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_traj</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">dim_x</span><span class="p">))</span>
    <span class="n">random_drift_grid_sample</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sqrt</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">step_size</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">random_drift_grid</span><span class="p">[:,</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">noise</span>
    
    <span class="c1">#Initialize list of trajectory:</span>
    <span class="n">x_traj</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">x_start</span><span class="p">]</span>
    
    
    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">time</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">tqdm</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">enumerate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">)):</span>
        
        <span class="c1">#Get last location and time</span>
        <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span>
        <span class="n">t</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nb">float</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">])</span>
        
        <span class="c1">#Get deterministic drift and random drift sample</span>
        <span class="n">determ_drift</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">step_size</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">f_determ_drift</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">random_drift_sample</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">random_drift_grid_sample</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span>
        
        <span class="c1">#Compute next step:</span>
        <span class="n">next_step</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">determ_drift</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">random_drift_sample</span>
        
        <span class="c1">#Save step:</span>
        <span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">append</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">next_step</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">stack</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="n">time_grid</span>    
</pre></div> </body></html> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p><em>Note: There are fancier (but much less intuitive) methods to compute solutions other than the Euler-Maryuama method. This is beyond the scope of this tutorial.</em></p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <h3 id="2.1.-Define-Example-Random-Drift-Functions-g">2.1. Define Example Random Drift Functions g<a class="anchor-link" href="#2.1.-Define-Example-Random-Drift-Functions-g">¶</a></h3> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Let's define two example drift functions and plot them:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Linear</strong>: $g(t)=0.1+0.05t$</li> <li><strong>Periodic</strong>: $g(t)=\sin(2\pi t)+1.10$</li> </ul> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell "> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"> <div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt">In [4]:</div> <div class="jp-CodeMirrorEditor jp-Editor jp-InputArea-editor" data-type="inline"> <div class="CodeMirror cm-s-jupyter"> <div class=" highlight hl-ipython3"><pre><span></span><span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">linear_g</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">constant</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mf">0.2</span><span class="p">):</span>
    <span class="sd">"""t - 1d np.ndarray or float</span>
<span class="sd">    Returns: 1d np.ndarray or float"""</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="mf">0.1</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="n">constant</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">t</span>

<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">periodic_g</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">):</span>
    <span class="sd">"""t - 1d np.ndarray or float</span>
<span class="sd">    Returns: 1d np.ndarray or float"""</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sqrt</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">sin</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">pi</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="mf">1.10</span><span class="p">)</span>

<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">plot_g_random_drift</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">drift_func_list</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">List</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">Callable</span><span class="p">],</span> <span class="n">min_t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">max_t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">5.0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">10000</span><span class="p">):</span>
    <span class="sd">"""Function to plot a random drift function g."""</span>
    <span class="n">fig</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">axs</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">plt</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">subplots</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">drift_func_list</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="n">figsize</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">drift_func_list</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">))</span>
    <span class="n">time</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">linspace</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">min_t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">max_t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">drift_func</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="nb">enumerate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">drift_func_list</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">plot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">drift_func</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time</span><span class="p">))</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_title</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">drift_func</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="vm">__name__</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_xlabel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"time"</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_ylabel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"g"</span><span class="p">)</span>

Define Example Deterministic Drift Functions f<a class="anchor-link" href="#2.2.-Define-Example-Deterministic-Drift-Functions-f">¶</a></h3> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Let's define example drift functions $f$:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Shift</strong>: $f(x,t)=-(x-4)$</li> <li><strong>Periodic</strong>: $f(x,t)=\cos(2\pi t^2)\cos(2\pi x^2)$</li> </ul> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell "> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"> <div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt">In [5]:</div> <div class="jp-CodeMirrorEditor jp-Editor jp-InputArea-editor" data-type="inline"> <div class="CodeMirror cm-s-jupyter"> <div class=" highlight hl-ipython3"><pre><span></span><span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">shift_f</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">shift</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mf">4.0</span><span class="p">):</span>
    <span class="sd">"""x - shape (n,k): a space coefficients </span>
<span class="sd">       t - shape (n) or float: time coefficients"""</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="o">-</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="n">shift</span><span class="p">)</span>

<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">periodic_f</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">):</span>
    <span class="sd">"""x - shape (n,k): space coefficients </span>
<span class="sd">       t - shape (n) or float: time coefficients"""</span>

    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="nb">isinstance</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="nb">float</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cos</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">pi</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="o">**</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cos</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">pi</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="p">))</span> <span class="c1">#*normalizer[:,None])</span>
    <span class="k">else</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cos</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">pi</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="o">**</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">)[:,</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">cos</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">pi</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="o">**</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">))</span> <span class="c1">#*normalizer[:,None])</span>

<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">plot_f_determ_drift</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">determ_func_list</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">List</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">Callable</span><span class="p">],</span>
                <span class="n">min_t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> 
                <span class="n">max_t</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">2.5</span><span class="p">,</span> 
                <span class="n">min_x</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span>
                <span class="n">max_x</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">2.5</span><span class="p">,</span>
                <span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1000</span><span class="p">,</span>
                <span class="n">plot_contours</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">False</span><span class="p">):</span>
    <span class="sd">"""Function to plot the function f(x,t) in an Ito-SDE."""</span>
    <span class="n">time</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">linspace</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">min_t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">max_t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">oned_grid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">linspace</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">min_x</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">max_x</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="n">twod_grid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">([[</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">x</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">product</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">oned_grid</span><span class="p">)])</span>
    <span class="n">extent</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">min_x</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">max_x</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">min_t</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">max_t</span><span class="p">]</span>
    
    <span class="n">fig</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">axs</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">plt</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">subplots</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">determ_func_list</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="n">figsize</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="o">*</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">determ_func_list</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">))</span>
    
    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">determ_func</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="nb">enumerate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">determ_func_list</span><span class="p">):</span>
        <span class="n">derivative</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">determ_func</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">twod_grid</span><span class="p">[:,</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">reshape</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="n">twod_grid</span><span class="p">[:,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">])</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">imshow</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">derivative</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">reshape</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">transpose</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="n">interpolation</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'bilinear'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">origin</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'lower'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">extent</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">extent</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cmap</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">plt</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">get_cmap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'YlOrRd'</span><span class="p">))</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">plot_contours</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">contour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">derivative</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">reshape</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_grid_points</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">transpose</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="n">interpolation</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'bilinear'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">origin</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'lower'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">extent</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">extent</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'black'</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_title</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">determ_func</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="vm">__name__</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_xlabel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"time t"</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_ylabel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"location x"</span><span class="p">)</span>

<span class="n">plot_f_determ_drift</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">shift_f</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">periodic_f</span><span class="p">])</span>

class="n">initial_dist</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="nb">str</span> <span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"normal"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">t_end</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mf">4.0</span><span class="p">):</span>
    <span class="sd">"""Function to animate and plot a 1d SDE over time."""</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">initial_dist</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="s2">"normal"</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="n">x_start</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">random</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">normal</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">n_samples</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">reshape</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span>
    <span class="k">elif</span> <span class="n">initial_dist</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="s2">"uniform"</span><span class="p">:</span>
        <span class="n">x_start</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">random</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">uniform</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">size</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">n_samples</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">reshape</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="n">x_traj</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">squeeze</span><span class="p">()</span>
    
    <span class="n">fig</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">axs</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">plt</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">subplots</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">figsize</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">24</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">36</span><span class="p">))</span>
    <span class="n">camera</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">Camera</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">fig</span><span class="p">)</span>
    
    <span class="n">oned_grid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">linspace</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">min</span><span class="p">(),</span> <span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">max</span><span class="p">(),</span> <span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">))</span>
    <span class="n">twod_grid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">np</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">([[</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">x</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">product</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">oned_grid</span><span class="p">)])</span>
    <span class="n">extent</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">[</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">min</span><span class="p">(),</span> <span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">max</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">min</span><span class="p">(),</span> <span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">max</span><span class="p">()]</span>
    <span class="n">derivative</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">f_drift</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">twod_grid</span><span class="p">[:,</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">reshape</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="n">twod_grid</span><span class="p">[:,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">])</span>
    <span class="n">derivative_plot</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">derivative</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">reshape</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">))</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">transpose</span><span class="p">()</span>
    
    <span class="n">g_drift_per_time</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">g_drift</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">)</span>

    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">idx</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">tqdm</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">range</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="nb">max</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">int</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nb">len</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">))):</span>
    
        <span class="c1">#Plot evolution over time over deterministic drift:</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">imshow</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">derivative_plot</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">interpolation</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'bilinear'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">origin</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'lower'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">extent</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">extent</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cmap</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">plt</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">get_cmap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'YlOrRd'</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="n">aspect</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'auto'</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">idx</span><span class="o">></span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">:</span>
            <span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">idy</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="nb">range</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">):</span>
                <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">plot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">[:</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="p">[:</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">idy</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">squeeze</span><span class="p">())</span> <span class="c1">#,label=sample_labels)</span>
            <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">plot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">[:</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="p">[:</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">squeeze</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">axis</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s1">'black'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">linewidth</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_title</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"Example trajectories (color=f)"</span><span class="p">)</span>

        <span class="c1">#Plot distribution:</span>
        <span class="n">sns</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">kdeplot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x_traj</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="n">ax</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">])</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_title</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"Distribution of X_t"</span><span class="p">)</span>

        <span class="c1">#Plot random drift:</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">plot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">time_grid</span><span class="p">[:</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="n">g_drift_per_time</span><span class="p">[:</span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">])</span>
        <span class="n">axs</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">set_title</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"Random drift g"</span><span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="n">camera</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">snap</span><span class="p">()</span>
        
    <span class="n">animation</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">camera</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">animate</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="c1"># animation ready</span>
    <span class="n">plt</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">close</span><span class="p">()</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">animation</span>
</pre></div> </body></html> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Set hyperparameters.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell jp-mod-noOutputs "> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"> <div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt">In [7]:</div> <div class="jp-CodeMirrorEditor jp-Editor jp-InputArea-editor" data-type="inline"> <div class="CodeMirror cm-s-jupyter"> <div class=" highlight hl-ipython3"><pre><span></span><span class="n">RUN_ANIMATION</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">False</span>

Run first simple SDE<a class="anchor-link" href="#2.4.-Run-first-simple-SDE">¶</a></h3> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>Let's set:</p> <ul> <li>$X_0\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$</li> <li>$f(x,t)=-(x-4)$</li> <li>$g(t)=\sin(2\pi t)+1.10$</li> </ul> <p>and run the SDE.</p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell jp-MarkdownCell jp-Notebook-cell"> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"><div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt"> </div><div class="jp-RenderedHTMLCommon jp-RenderedMarkdown jp-MarkdownOutput " data-mime-type="text/markdown"> <p>The below animation shows:</p> <ul> <li>Top figure: 5 example trajectories (plot over the function $f(x,t)$)</li> <li>Middle figure: the change of distribution over time</li> <li>Bottom figure: the change in drift $g(t)$ over time.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </div> </div><div class="jp-Cell jp-CodeCell jp-Notebook-cell "> <div class="jp-Cell-inputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-InputCollapser jp-Cell-inputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-InputArea jp-Cell-inputArea"> <div class="jp-InputPrompt jp-InputArea-prompt">In [8]:</div> <div class="jp-CodeMirrorEditor jp-Editor jp-InputArea-editor" data-type="inline"> <div class="CodeMirror cm-s-jupyter"> <div class=" highlight hl-ipython3"><pre><span></span><span class="n">fpath</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"simple_sde.mp4"</span>
<span class="n">animation</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">animate_ito_sde</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">shift_f</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">periodic_g</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_steps</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">N_STEPS</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">n_samples</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">N_SAMPLES</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="n">animation</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">save</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">fpath</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="n">HTML</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">animation</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">to_html5_video</span><span class="p">())</span>
</pre></div> </body></html> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="jp-Cell-outputWrapper"> <div class="jp-Collapser jp-OutputCollapser jp-Cell-outputCollapser"> </div> <div class="jp-OutputArea
